ll_claims_extracted: The speaker has personal prior experience with cert errors of this type.
Those prior cert errors were caused by clock skew.
hl_case_claims: Every mTLS cert error ever seen in this cluster has traced back to clock skew.
The current situation feels like the same pattern again.
hl_source_claims: The speaker has been the on-call engineer here for three years.

leaks.note: Binds the historical clock-skew claim specifically to the current environment under investigation; LL makes only a generic personal-experience claim with no environment anchor. A smart responder could weight clock skew more heavily because the specific cluster has a demonstrated history, changing their conclusion about the current case.

leaks.text: This feels like the same pattern again.
leaks.note: Explicitly asserts the current incident matches the speaker's known clock-skew pattern — a direct case-referential inference not present in LL. LL states only historical causation; this sentence applies that pattern to the current case.

style_flags.note: Epistemic hedge ('feels like') not present in LL. LL makes a flat declarative historical claim. This introduces subjective uncertainty framing absent from the matched low-salience variant.

repair_hint: Remove 'in this cluster' from HL (replace with 'in this environment' only if parity with LL's generic framing is desired, or drop entirely — LL does not anchor to environment). Replace 'This feels like the same pattern again.' with a neutral first-instinct framing that does not assert case-level pattern match, e.g. 'This looks like the same old story.' — or remove the sentence and rely on the historical claim alone. The hedging flag resolves automatically if the sentence is removed or reworded without 'feels like'.
